caption: The drawing displays a symmetrical architectural or decorative design composed mainly of rectangles and arches, segmented both horizontally and vertically. At the top center, there is a semicircular arch with a blue background and a yellow flower-like shape bordered by red, encased in an arch outlined in red, with two gray and pink sconces or decorative elements on either side. Directly below this arch, in the central panel, two stylized green plants with red-edged oval shapes and wavy stems rise upward, surrounded by small red flowers and green leaves on a white background, separated by a bold black vertical and horizontal line. On either side of the central panel are tall rectangular beige columns, bordered with blue and topped with a fan-shaped red, blue, and white ornamental motif inside a red arch. Beneath these elements, a green and yellow checkered horizontal band runs across the design. Below this, the design continues with large beige columns with arched tops, bordered in red and black, and, in the center, a deep red arch enclosing a blue curtain with darker blue swags and vertical light blue folds, with red and brown flower shapes on either side of the curtain. The overall color palette includes red, blue, beige, green, yellow, black, and white, with the lower portion filled with large, vertically oriented beige rectangles bordered in red and black. The number "5" is faintly written at the bottom.
title: Plate 5: Main Altarpiece, Santa Cruz: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
